extracted.intended_audience: ProofWiki contributors and editors (people writing or editing pages on ProofWiki)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical FAQ and house-style rules for contributing, formatting, and refactoring pages on ProofWiki, including LaTeX/template conventions and how to organize proofs and sources. Intended to guide editors on acceptable edits, page structure, and technical quirks of the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs on subpages for unambiguous reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs (and definitions) are placed on appropriate sub-pages so each part/proof can be unambiguously referenced internally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each part of a theorem (e.g. 'First Part') and each separate proof often has a blue heading link to a subpage (e.g. 'Fundamental Theorem of Calculus/First Part'). The proof(s) of that part are gathered on that subpage. This allows referencing a particular proof without risking circular dependencies (e.g. a proof depending on its own result).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to house notation style
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not change notation indiscriminately; the site uses a particular house style of notation chosen to be unambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There will always be multiple notations; ProofWiki insists on a particular style. If you believe your notation is superior, communicate reasons rather than unilaterally changing it. The maintainers prefer not to change notation unless there are good reasons (they take care to select a notation first and foremost unambiguous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise site-content questions on the wiki (not external email)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use relevant talk pages or the site's Help:Questions instead of emailing administrators for content questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emailing creates no public record, may not get answered reliably, and prevents the community from contributing to an answer. Use the associated talk page or, if necessary, the user's talk page to discuss specific points with a user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not delete existing proofs; add additional proofs as separate subpages
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a better proof, add it as an additional proof rather than replacing an existing one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow multiple proofs for a theorem by putting each separate proof into its own subpage and transcluding them into the main page. Deleting others' proofs is considered rude. If you object to a proof, raise it on the associated talk page so the author can be consulted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \left and \right grouping in LaTeX
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforce pairing of \left and \right (and grouping braces) in LaTeX to avoid parsing/editing problems and to ensure parentheses size appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The curly braces are grouping indications for TeX and ensure every \left is paired with the intended \right; this simplifies finding omitted/extra braces when editing. It avoids problems with copy-pasting and ensures parentheses size appropriately when content grows/shrinks. Exceptions: simple equation references like (1) and (3′). Note: this rule has been partly superseded by custom LaTeX commands (see Symbols:LaTeX Commands/ProofWiki Specific).

rubrics_metrics.name: One sentence per line
rubrics_metrics.description: Write proofs with one sentence per line to improve readability and make argument flow clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rigid stylistic practice breaks arguments into well-defined steps so information is assimilated more easily on the website. It contrasts with printed textbooks (which economize space). Although it may look simplistic, it's a deliberate practice to aid clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert extra blank line(s) between sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections should be spread out with two blank lines at the end of every section before the next header (with few specialised exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This house style increases ease of reading. Because MediaWiki removes extra blank lines when you edit an individual section, editing single sections is discouraged; to preserve blank lines you may need to edit the whole page. The site policy favors keeping pages small to reduce this problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve redirects until all incoming links updated
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep redirects from old page titles rather than deleting them immediately when renaming pages, unless the redirect is brand new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before deleting a redirect, ensure every page that links to it has been updated (use 'What links here'). Deleting redirects prematurely can break internal links and external sites' links. If the redirect is from a very recent rename (e.g. a simple typo fix), it is usual to delete that redirect after renaming because few external links will exist. Policy has evolved toward deleting redirects as soon as pages linking to them are appropriately redirected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign your posts on talk pages
rubrics_metrics.description: When posting on talk pages, sign and timestamp your post to record who said what and when.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the signature button (--~~~~) which inserts a user signature and timestamp. This is required for discussion pages (not main pages like definitions or proofs) so that conversation can be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain 'Sources' section flow and links
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources sections often implement a linear 'previous'/'next' reading flow; edits must preserve or correctly update these links or invoke SourceReview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you change the name of a page or copy a page with such citations, you must ensure the source flow is not compromised. If flow may be compromised, add the {{SourceReview}} template to the page. When copying content, remove the citation unless the new page truly corresponds to the material in the cited source. If it does correspond, amend the source-flow links (including on neighboring pages) or invoke SourceReview so maintainers can fix the links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refactoring requires pages to be standalone and careful handling of transclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: When refactoring (splitting pages into subpages and transcluding them), ensure new subpages are standalone and handle theorem statements, transclusion tags, and citations properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If extracting proofs into e.g. 'Proof 1' and 'Proof 2' subpages, also extract the theorem statement and place it at the top of the new page; the proof should be wrapped in onlyinclude tags so that only the proof is transcluded into the master page. At the bottom of pages, source citations must be attended to to avoid compromising linear source flow. Because of these complexities, refactoring is considered best left to experienced editors (experienced in ProofWiki's house style and linking philosophy). New contributors are requested not to embark on refactoring until familiar with site conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition vs equivalence: implement as definition only if source uses that form
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to implement an alternative form of a concept as a Definition page or as an equivalence theorem based on whether the concept appears in hard-copy sources in that specific form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the concept can be found in a hard copy of a source work in that specific form, implement it as a definition. If not, implement it as a theorem-and-proof demonstrating equivalence. If you do implement it as a definition, you must provide an independent proof that this definition is equivalent to existing definitions (showing equivalence to just one existing definition is sufficient if the other definitions are already known to be mutually equivalent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid template/parser conflicts in LaTeX (eqn template)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the {{eqn}} template, avoid including raw MediaWiki template delimiters {{ }} or parameter bars | inside LaTeX without escaping or spacing to prevent the MediaWiki parser from breaking the LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MediaWiki template parser takes precedence over MathJax and will interpret {{ and }} as template invocations and | as parameter separators. Workarounds: put a conventional space between braces so that {{ and }} become { { and } } in source; replace | with \vert, || and \| with \Vert (or use appropriate TeX commands) to avoid parser misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use {{=}} template when you need a literal '=' inside template parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: When a maintenance template's parameter needs to include a literal dollar-sign-equals-dollar expression (e.g. 'Why does $a = b$?'), use the {{=}} helper template to avoid parser confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without this workaround the parser may interpret the '=' as part of a parameter name. Example: use {{explain|Why does $a {{=}} b$?}} so the '=' appears correctly in the output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referrals for large tasks (downloading the entire site) and use of maintenance templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Downloading the entire site with functional visuals (CSS/MathJax) is possible but requires considerable effort; discuss the approach on the relevant talk page and use maintenance templates when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempts with generic website downloaders often produce pages with no CSS or non-working MathJax. The FAQ suggests that producing a full offline copy 'needs considerable tedious hard slog' and to discuss the process on the talk page; when the work is complete, remove the {{Finish}} tag and optionally add a {{Proofread}} call for review.
